The highest point in the United States is Denali (also known as Mount McKinley) in Alaska, with a summit elevation of 20,310 feet (6,190 m) above sea level [d2][d6][d10]. It is also the highest peak in all of North America [d1][d10]. For those interested in the contiguous United States (the lower 48 states), the highest point is Mount Whitney in California's Sierra Nevada, at approximately 14,494–14,505 feet above sea level [d3][d8][d9]. Additionally, Hawaii's Mauna Kea, while lower in elevation above sea level, is sometimes considered the tallest mountain on Earth when measured from its base on the ocean floor, with a total height of over 33,000 feet [d2][d1].
